text: Given a valid user_id and no optional parameters, When graph_create_tap is called, Then it returns a Temporary Access Pass usable exactly once within its lifetime window
Given is_usable_once=false and an explicit lifetime_minutes, When graph_create_tap is called, Then the returned pass's settings match what was requested
Given a non-existent user_id, When graph_create_tap is called, Then a structured not-found error is returned, not a raw exception
Given a shared mailbox and a delegate without SendOnBehalf rights, When exo_add_sendonbehalf_permission is called, Then the delegate is granted SendOnBehalf on that mailbox

Given the mocked-cmdlet test above passes, When the same call is made against a real INT tenant mailbox, Then exo_get_mailbox confirms the delegate appears under GrantSendOnBehalfTo after EXO's replication delay
steps: Pick a test shared mailbox and a test delegate user on the INT tenant
Wait a few minutes for EXO replication
expect: delegate's UPN/alias appears in the mailbox's GrantSendOnBehalfTo list

text: Given a mailbox and two new alias addresses passed in one call, When exo_add_email_alias is called, Then both are added and existing primary/alias addresses are unchanged

Given an alias address already assigned to a different recipient in the tenant, When exo_add_email_alias is called with it, Then Exchange's rejection is surfaced for that address rather than silently dropped

Given the Add-hashtable wire format assumption in Tech design §B option analysis, When exo_add_email_alias / exo_add_sendonbehalf_permission are first run against the real EXO REST endpoint, Then confirm whether {"Add": [...]} is accepted as-is or the read-merge-write fallback is needed
steps: Call exo_add_email_alias against a disposable test mailbox on the INT tenant
Inspect the raw HTTP response/status from the EXO REST endpoint
If rejected, switch the implementation to the read-merge-write fallback documented in Tech design §B
expect: either a 200-class success with the alias actually added (confirmed via exo_get_mailbox), or a specific rejection reason that tells us to use the fallback

text: Given a group id and a user id not currently an owner, When graph_add_group_owner is called, Then the user becomes an owner
Given the same call repeated for a user already an owner, When graph_add_group_owner is called again, Then the tool reports an already-satisfied state rather than a failure

Given the mocked 400-handling test above assumes a specific Graph error message shape, When the same call is made against a real tenant with an already-owner user, Then confirm the actual error message text/shape matches what the mocked test assumes
steps: Add a test user as owner of a test group on the INT tenant
Call graph_add_group_owner again for the same group/user pair
Inspect the raw Graph error response
expect: either the existing graph_assign_groups-style 'already exist' text match works unchanged, or the handling needs adjusting to the real error text

text: Given a valid language tag, When passed to graph_create_user, Then a subsequent graph_get_user shows that preferredLanguage
Given a valid language tag, When passed to graph_update_user on an existing user, Then a subsequent graph_get_user shows the updated preferredLanguage

Given the 5 new tools/params, When their implementations are code-reviewed, Then none accepts a tenant-id-like parameter or any other cross-tenant override -- isolation is 100% inherited from the existing per-request credential wiring
steps: Read the final diff for all 5 changes across both repos
Confirm no new parameter resembles a tenant/org override (e.g. tenant_id, org_id, directory override)
Confirm every new/changed function still goes through the existing client_factory()/ExoClient per-request credential path with no alternate code path
expect: no cross-tenant override surface found in the diff

text: Given the platform has not yet granted UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite.All / Group.ReadWrite.All and the tenant has not re-consented (see Tech design SS8), When graph_create_tap or graph_add_group_owner is called pre-rollout, Then confirm the 403 is clearly distinguishable from a 403 caused by a genuinely missing/invalid user_id or group_id, so the rollout dependency does not get misdiagnosed as a code bug
steps: Before the platform-side scope grant lands, call graph_create_tap and graph_add_group_owner against a valid user/group on a real tenant
Record the exact Graph error code/message
After the scope grant + tenant re-consent, repeat the same call and confirm it now succeeds
expect: pre-rollout 403 text is recognizably a permission/consent issue (matches the precedent documented in this repo's README for Mail.Read/Calendars.ReadWrite rollouts), not confusable with a not-found error
